it's actually against the law for companies to add hurdles to/remove the ability to block users, see here- https://www.gov.uk/guidance/a-guide-to-the-online-safety-bill#adults-will-have-more-control-over-the-content-they-see

also, the guidelines for both the App Store and the Google Play Store require that user-generated content must be able to be blocked in any app they offer, so restricting/granting the ability to block a person based on a reason would violate app store TOS and end with the app being completely removed from marketplaces
@{6619d83b90c9fcb83aa82595|full_name} im not opening that

@{62a26724d11dd80b9cf67308|full_name} I'll summarise for you, it's now law that blocking needs to be accessible and effective for both adult and underage users. It would be violating the Online Safety Bill (2022) to add additional hurdles or a 'good enough reason' to blocking/voting to remove users from a room. 

This bill protects users through a 'triple shed', one of the three requirements being that any platform that is accessible in the UK must have the ability to control the content you see, and have access to tools like blocking or muting etc in order to control what you see, hear and interact with- 'services must also empower their users with tools that give them greater control over the content that they see and who they engage with.'

it says, 'The largest platforms will be required to offer users tools so they can have greater control over the kinds of content they see and who they engage with online. These platforms must also proactively offer these tools to all their registered users, so it is easy for them to decide whether to use these tools or not. The tools must be effective and easy to access and could include human moderation, blocking content flagged by other internet users or sensitivity and warning screens.' 

This is regulated and enforced by OFCOM. OFCOM has the power to take appropriate action against all social media and tech companies, no matter where they are based, if they are accessible to UK users. Companies that don't adhere to these rules are liable for fines of up to 18 million or 10% of their global turnover, whichever is higher.

realistically this isn't happening no matter how badly you want to know why someone blocked you.
